name: PineconeUpsert
title: Pinecone Upsert
description: Store text in a Pinecone index, letting Pinecone do the embedding
whenToUse: Write passages into a Pinecone index so they can be found by meaning later: building or topping up a knowledge base, indexing documents for retrieval. Takes text and stores it; the index must have been created with an embedding model attached. Long documents should be split into passages before this step, since it stores each record whole.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Trigger signal from the upstream node

outputs.name: ids
outputs.description: The record ids that were written, in the order they were sent

indexName.title: Index Name
indexName.description: The Pinecone index to write to. It must have been created with an embedding model attached, since the text is embedded by Pinecone rather than beforehand.

namespace.title: Namespace
namespace.description: Write into one namespace. Leave blank for the index's default namespace.

textField.title: Text Field Name
textField.description: The field the index embeds, from its field_map. Get this wrong and Pinecone accepts the record, embeds nothing, and reports no error, so it is worth checking against the index rather than assuming.

records.title: Records
records.description: A batch from an upstream step: an array of objects with text, and optionally _id and metadata. Takes precedence over the single-record fields below. An expression, e.g. "return signal.split1.passages".

text.title: Text
text.description: The passage to store, when writing a single record. Ignored if Records is set.

vectorId.title: Record ID
vectorId.description: A stable id for the single record. Reusing an id UPDATES that record rather than adding another, which is how a re-run avoids duplicating everything. Leave blank and one is generated positionally, which does not survive a re-run.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Extra fields stored alongside the text and filterable at search time, e.g. "return { source: signal.doc.url }". Field names cannot collide with the id or the text field; those always win.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: pinecone
package.packageFile:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/package.schema.json

name: pinecone
displayName: Pinecone
version: 2.0.0
description: Vector search over Pinecone, with embedding done by Pinecone

# WHY THIS PACKAGE COULD FINALLY BECOME A MANIFEST, and why the reason was not the one
# recorded in the backlog for months.
#
# The blocker was never "Pinecone has no REST API" — it always had one. It was that the old
# nodes CONSUMED an embedding service over a service edge: query and upload both took a
# vector from a neighbouring embedding node, and no manifest call can make that hop. Adding
# REST would not have helped, because the missing piece was upstream of the request.
#
# Pinecone's INTEGRATED INFERENCE removes the hop entirely. An index created with an
# embedding model attached accepts TEXT and embeds it server-side, so `/records/*` takes the
# raw string and there is no vector to source from anywhere. The service edge disappears
# rather than being expressed.
#
# THE COST, and it is a real one: integrated inference only works on an index created WITH a
# model and a field_map. An index holding externally-computed vectors cannot use these
# endpoints. Repointing an existing workflow means recreating the index, which is why the
# node types changed rather than being reused (see each node.yaml).

category: storage
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749139513/gravity/icons/pinecone.png

allowedHosts:
  # The control plane, where an index is looked up by name.
  - api.pinecone.io
  # The DATA plane host is per-index and only learned at run time — a name like
  # `kb-a1b2c3.svc.aped-4627-b74a.pinecone.io`. Two labels deep, so `*.pinecone.io` (one
  # level only) would refuse it: `**` is required and is the weaker rule on purpose. Still
  # bounded to Pinecone's own domain, which is what allowedHosts is for.
  - "**.pinecone.io"

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.7.0"
  credential: [apiKeyHeader]
  transport: [json]
  # Pinecone's record upsert takes newline-delimited JSON: one document per line, no array.
  encoding: [ndjson]

credentials.pineconeCredential.yaml:
# One key. The retired credential also carried an `environment` field ("us-east-1-aws"),
# which the old SDK needed to build a host. The REST path looks the index up by name on the
# control plane and is TOLD its host, so asking for the environment as well would be asking
# for something already known, and getting it wrong produced a confusing DNS failure rather
# than a useful message.

name: pineconeCredential
displayName: Pinecone
description: >-
  Pinecone API key, from the console under API Keys. The key's project must contain the
  index the node names.

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Pinecone API key
    placeholder: "pcsk_..."

shared.index.yaml:
# THE HOST LOOKUP, shared because every node in this package needs it and none can skip it.
#
# Pinecone's data plane lives on a host that is unique per index and not derivable from the
# index name: `kb-a1b2c3.svc.aped-4627-b74a.pinecone.io`. The old SDK hid this behind
# `pinecone.index(name)`, which is why the retired nodes only ever asked for a NAME.
#
# Keeping that config field is worth one extra request. The alternative is making an author
# paste a host they have to go and find, and which changes if the index is recreated.

describe:
  name: describeIndex
  method: GET
  url: "https://api.pinecone.io/indexes/{{ config.indexName }}"
  transport: json
  credential: { $ref: index#credential }
  headers:
    X-Pinecone-Api-Version: "2025-04"
  error:
    # A 404 here means the index does not exist IN THIS KEY'S PROJECT, which is the single
    # most common setup mistake: the right name in the wrong project. Said plainly, because
    # the raw reply is a generic not-found that sends people looking at the wrong thing.
    when: "return !response.host"
    message: >-
      return 'Pinecone index "' + config.indexName + '" was not found, or the API key belongs
      to a different project. Check the index name and that this key is from the same project.'

# apiKeyHeader rather than bearer: Pinecone reads `Api-Key`, and a bearer token is silently
# ignored rather than rejected, so the failure looks like a permissions problem.
credential:
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: Api-Key
  value: "{{ credentials.pineconeCredential.apiKey }}"

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml's order.

- emit: upserted
  value: "return Number(response.upsertedCount) || 0"

# RECOMPUTED FROM THE CONFIG, not read from the reply, because Pinecone's upsert returns only
# a count. The derivation repeats the id rule in run.yaml, and it has to: an events row
# cannot see the body that was sent, and the ids are the only handle a later run has on these
# records. If the id rule in run.yaml changes, this must change with it.
- emit: ids
  value: >-
    return (
      Array.isArray(config.records) && config.records.length
        ? config.records
        : [{ text: config.text, _id: config.vectorId }]
    )
      .filter(r => String((r && (r.text || r.chunk_text)) || '').trim().length > 0)
      .map((r, i) => String((r && (r._id || r.id)) || config.vectorId || ('rec-' + (i + 1))))
files.api/run.yaml:
# TWO CALLS: learn the index's host, then write to it. Same host lookup as the search node.

- $ref: index#describe

- name: upsert
  method: POST

  url: >-
    return 'https://' + calls.describeIndex.host + '/records/namespaces/'
      + encodeURIComponent(String(config.namespace || '').trim() || '__default__')
      + '/upsert'

  transport: json

  # NEWLINE-DELIMITED JSON: one record per line, no array, no commas. `JSON.stringify` of
  # the same array is valid JSON and a 400 here, because Pinecone parses line by line. This
  # is the reason `encoding: ndjson` exists rather than the body being joined by hand in an
  # expression: a record whose text contains a newline has to stay on one line, and only the
  # serializer can guarantee that.
  encoding: ndjson

  credential: { $ref: index#credential }
  headers:
    X-Pinecone-Api-Version: "2025-04"

  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

  # ONE OR MANY, from the same manifest. `records` (an array from an upstream step) wins when
  # present; otherwise the single text/id/metadata fields build one record. The retired node
  # had the same two modes, and collapsing them into one shape here means a workflow that
  # grows from one document to a batch does not change node.
  body: >-
    return ((rows) => rows
      .map((r, i) => Object.assign(
        {},
        // Stored metadata first, so a field it happens to contain can never overwrite the
        // id or the text below. Silent corruption of the embedded field is the worst case
        // this ordering prevents.
        (r && typeof r.metadata === 'object' && r.metadata) ? r.metadata : {},
        {
          // Pinecone needs a stable id per record. An author-supplied one lets a later run
          // UPDATE rather than duplicate; without one there is nothing meaningful to derive,
          // so a positional fallback at least keeps a single batch internally unique.
          _id: String((r && (r._id || r.id)) || config.vectorId || ('rec-' + (i + 1))),
          // The field name must match the index's field_map, or Pinecone stores the record
          // and embeds NOTHING — it is accepted, unsearchable, and reports no error.
          [String(config.textField || 'chunk_text')]: String((r && (r.text || r.chunk_text)) || '')
        }
      ))
      .filter(r => String(r[String(config.textField || 'chunk_text')] || '').trim().length > 0)
    )(
      Array.isArray(config.records) && config.records.length
        ? config.records
        : [{ text: config.text, metadata: config.metadata, _id: config.vectorId }]
    )

  error:
    # The reply is `{ upsertedCount }`. A zero means every record was filtered out as empty,
    # which is a silent no-op worth failing on: the workflow ran, wrote nothing, and would
    # otherwise report success.
    when: "return !response || Number(response.upsertedCount) === 0"
    message: >-
      return 'Pinecone stored no records. Every record had empty text, or the text field name
      does not match the index (this node sent "'
      + String(config.textField || 'chunk_text') + '").'
files.config.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/config.schema.json

# CHUNKING IS GONE, and this is the one thing lost in the migration rather than simplified.
#
# The retired node had enableChunking / chunkingStrategy / maxChunkSize / chunkOverlap: it
# split a long document into overlapping passages and stored each. That is a text algorithm,
# not a request, and expressing it as an expression would have meant a paragraph-splitting
# loop nobody could read or debug inside a YAML string.
#
# So the node stores what it is given, and splitting belongs upstream. Named here rather
# than quietly dropped, because a workflow that used chunking and is repointed at this node
# will store whole documents as single records, retrieval quality will fall, and nothing
# will report an error. If chunking is wanted back it should be its own node, where it can
# be tested on its own terms.

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [indexName]
  properties:
    indexName:
      type: string
      title: Index Name
      description: >-
        The Pinecone index to write to. It must have been created with an embedding model
        attached, since the text is embedded by Pinecone rather than beforehand.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    namespace:
      type: string
      title: Namespace
      description: Write into one namespace. Leave blank for the index's default namespace.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    textField:
      type: string
      title: Text Field Name
      description: >-
        The field the index embeds, from its field_map. Get this wrong and Pinecone accepts
        the record, embeds nothing, and reports no error, so it is worth checking against
        the index rather than assuming.
      default: chunk_text
      ui:field: template

    records:
      type: array
      title: Records
      description: >-
        A batch from an upstream step: an array of objects with text, and optionally _id and
        metadata. Takes precedence over the single-record fields below. An expression, e.g.
        "return signal.split1.passages".
      default: []

    text:
      type: string
      title: Text
      description: The passage to store, when writing a single record. Ignored if Records is set.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    vectorId:
      type: string
      title: Record ID
      description: >-
        A stable id for the single record. Reusing an id UPDATES that record rather than
        adding another, which is how a re-run avoids duplicating everything. Leave blank and
        one is generated positionally, which does not survive a re-run.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    metadata:
      type: object
      title: Metadata
      description: >-
        Extra fields stored alongside the text and filterable at search time, e.g.
        "return { source: signal.doc.url }". Field names cannot collide with the id or the
        text field; those always win.
      default: {}
"ui:order":
  [indexName, namespace, textField, records, text, vectorId, metadata]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    required: true
    description: Trigger signal from the upstream node

outputs:
  - name: upserted
    type: number
    description: How many records Pinecone stored

  # The ids are what makes a later run an UPDATE rather than a duplicate, so they are worth
  # emitting even though the vendor does not return them: a workflow that stores and then
  # needs to revise the same records has no other handle on them.
  - name: ids
    type: array
    description: The record ids that were written, in the order they were sent

credentials:
  - name: pineconeCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Pinecone
files.node.yaml:
$schema: https://docs.unoverse.ai/schemas/nodes/node.schema.json

# Transcribed from _legacy/nodes/pinecone/src/PineconeUpload. The embedding step is gone
# rather than reimplemented (Pinecone embeds server-side), and so is the chunking: see
# config.yaml, which explains why that one is a genuine loss rather than a simplification.

type: PineconeUpsert

# NOT the old `PineconeUpload`. Beyond the embedding change, this node no longer chunks long
# text, so a workflow silently repointed at it would start storing whole documents as single
# records and retrieval quality would drop with nothing reporting a problem.

kind: PromiseNode

name: Pinecone Upsert
category: Knowledge & Vectors
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749139513/gravity/icons/pinecone.png
color: "#4B5563"

description: Store text in a Pinecone index, letting Pinecone do the embedding

whenToUse: >-
  Write passages into a Pinecone index so they can be found by meaning later: building or
  topping up a knowledge base, indexing documents for retrieval. Takes text and stores it;
  the index must have been created with an embedding model attached. Long documents should
  be split into passages before this step, since it stores each record whole.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NEVER cacheable: this WRITES. Reusing a previous answer would report a successful upsert
  # for records that were never stored.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# WRITES to a real index. Uses a fixed id so re-running updates the same record instead of
# filling the index with test rows, which the retired fixture did not do.
#
# The batch form is exercised rather than the single-record one, because the batch path is
# where ndjson framing actually matters: one record produces one line and would pass even if
# the serializer wrongly emitted a JSON array.

testData:
  config:
    indexName: "{{ env.PINECONE_INDEX }}"
    textField: chunk_text
    # A LITERAL array, not a "return [...]" expression. A fixture supplies VALUES, in the
    # shape the config schema declares; an expression here would be checked as a string and
    # would reach the body resolver unevaluated.
    records:
      - _id: unoverse-node-test-1
        text: The return policy allows refunds within 30 days.
        metadata: { source: node-test }
      - _id: unoverse-node-test-2
        text: Damaged items are replaced free of charge.
        metadata: { source: node-test }
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    upserted: "return output.upserted === 2"
    ids: >-
      return Array.isArray(output.ids) && output.ids.length === 2
        && output.ids[0] === 'unoverse-node-test-1'
